name: All Egypt (National Composite 22°N–32°N)
biome: Nile Delta & Valley irrigated croplands + desert/coastal industrial basins
description: Complete Egypt national active-fire & thermal anomaly domain (254,175 harmonized rows across MODIS, S-NPP, NOAA-20, and NOAA-21 on a 0.05° × 0.05° grid).

name: Nile Delta & Greater Cairo (B30N_30E–B31N_31E)
biome: Intensive irrigated deltaic cropland (rice, wheat, maize)
description: Primary national agricultural fire concentration zone led by B30N_31E (7,926 cell-days), B31N_31E (4,101 cell-days), and B30N_30E (3,190 cell-days), peaking sharply in September–October.

name: Middle & Upper Egypt Nile Valley (B24N–B29N)
biome: Alluvial Nile corridor floodplain (sugarcane & winter wheat)
description: Linear agricultural corridor from Beni Suef and Minya (B28N_30E) through Assiut and Qena/Luxor (B25N_32E: 1,705 cell-days) to Aswan, with pronounced spring (MAM) harvest activity.

name: NW Coast, Alexandria West & Western Desert (B29N–B31N)
biome: Coastal Mediterranean steppe, hydrocarbon basins & desert oases
description: Encompasses West Alexandria industrial zone (B31N_29E), Matrouh/Western Desert basins (B30N_27E: 2,380 cell-days; B29N_27E: 1,833 cell-days), and Western oases.

name: Suez Gulf, Sinai & Red Sea Coast (B24N_33E–B31N_32E)
biome: Eastern Canal zone, Suez Gulf petrochemical corridor & Sinai
description: Covers Port Said/Ismailia/Suez (B30N_32E: 1,978 cell-days; B29N_32E: 1,929 cell-days) and Red Sea coastal blocks with high persistent static thermal source density.
